title: node lifecycle troubleshoot scratchpad
content:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent node flaps in prod-eu cluster since 2025-02-05. Nodes go NotReady and sometimes reboot within ~5–10 minutes. Several app pods stuck in ContainerCreating or CrashLoopBackOff. No recent deploys that align with the spike.

First quick triage (2/6):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  -> 3/12 NotReady, several show KubeletUnavailable, lastHeartbeat 2m ago
- kubectl describe node ip-10-20-7-45
  -> Conditions: Ready=False (Kubelet stopped posting status)
  -> Taints: none initially
  -> Events: "kubelet stopped posting status" repeated + "systemd: Stopped kubelet.service" on one host

Commands run and outputs (snippets):
- ssh ubuntu@ip-10-20-7-45 sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
  -> feb 05 03:12:21 kubelet[1234]: E0205 03:12:21.123456    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:XXX] Error: failed to register node "ip-10-20-7-45": Get "https://10.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/nodes/ip-10-20-7-45/status": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
  -> feb 05 03:12:22 kubelet[1234]: E0205 03:12:22.987654    1234 kubelet_pods.go:YYY] Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = \"failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed\"

- sudo dmesg | tail -n 80
  -> kernel: oom_killer invoked (killed process 2345 (containerd) total-vm:...)
  -> kernel: XFS warning: log is full, replay required

- sudo df -h /var/lib/containerd
  -> 95% used (suspect log / overlay growth)

- crictl ps -a
  -> many sandboxes in CREATED, failing to start

Hypotheses after initial pass:
1) Disk pressure (/var/lib) causing container runtime to fail and kubelet to crash -> triggers NotReady.
2) Containerd / runtime upgrade (automated image) caused OCI runtime incompatibility with current kernel.
3) CNI or MTU mismatch after underlying network change causing sandbox create to hang.
4) Cloud provider autoscale / image baking produced nodes with different kubelet certs / missing cloud-init steps.

Actions tried so far (what I did):
- Free up space: rm -rf /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/*/log && journalctl --vacuum-size=200M -> temporarily brought kubelet back up on 1 node.
- Rebooted 2 nodes (graceful) -> one came back and rejoined, one failed kubelet start due to containerd failing to start.
- sudo systemctl status containerd -> showed repeated errors: "failed to create shim task: runc did not start", plus overlay mount failures: "permission denied" on mount /var/lib/containerd/...
- Tried sudo apt-mark hold containerd to prevent an automatic package upgrade (found unattended-upgrades entry that had run on 2/5).
- Helm: inspected node bootstrap chart values (cluster-node-provisioner) -> noticed autoscaler.enabled=true and upgradeStrategy=Rolling, which could combine with OS unattended-upgrades to cause waves.
- kubectl cordon/drain on one flaky node before manual work: kubectl drain ip-10-20-7-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -> worked but pod eviction stuck on a few PVC-bound pods (timeout).

Relevant config/versions seen:
- kubelet: v1.28.4
- containerd: 1.7.3 -> matches artifact in AMI build but host had containerd 1.8.2 from unattended-upgrades on some nodes
- runc: 1.1.9
- kernel: 6.0.x (some nodes 5.15.x) -> mixed kernels across ASG (AMI redeploy with different kernel?)

Correlation notes:
- All failing nodes show containerd version 1.8.2 and kernel 6.0.x. Healthy nodes are containerd 1.7.3 + kernel 5.15.x.
- Unattended-upgrades ran around 02:00 UTC on those nodes per /var/log/unattended-upgrades.

Intermediate conclusion:
- Upgrade of containerd + newer kernel seems correlated with failures. OCI runtime incompat (overlay mount permissions / OOM) causing containerd to misbehave -> kubelet loses heartbeats.

Further commands to collect (next run):
- sudo tar czf /tmp/node-debug-$(hostname)-logs.tgz /var/log/{syslog,syslog.1} /var/log/unattended-upgrades /var/log/cloud-init.log /var/lib/containerd/*.log && upload to S3 (preserve for postmortem).
- sudo crictl logs <sandbox-id> (from crictl ps -a) for failing pod sandboxes.
- sudo containerd --version; sudo runc --version; cat /etc/os-release; uname -a; ls -l /var/lib/containerd/overlay2
- sudo ip link; ip route; sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables
- sudo journalctl -u unattended-upgrades -S "2025-02-05" - no-pager

Temporary mitigations applied (2/7):
- Put an ASG scale-in protection on current healthy nodes to avoid churn.
- Updated Helm chart values for cluster-node-provisioner to set unattended-upgrades=false and pin containerd package on AMI build pipeline (PR in cluster-provisioner repo). See linked PR.
- Added a temporary cluster-wide DaemonSet that checks containerd version and taints nodes with label node-provision/upgrade-needed=true if containerd != 1.7.3 so we can schedule remedial jobs. (rudimentary, removed once node fixed)

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Bake AMIs with explicit pinned package versions and disable unattended-upgrades for container runtime packages.
- Add preflight check in node bootstrap to verify runc/containerd runtime compatibility with kernel; fail node join instead of letting it become flaky.
- Improve alerts: differentiate kubelet crash vs network partition vs container runtime failure in SRE runbook.
- Make node-provisioner helm chart do safe rolling upgrades (maxUnavailable=1 and node drain backoff).

What actually resolved the immediate P0 (notes):
- Rolling back containerd on one failing host to 1.7.3 (via apt install containerd=1.7.3-+debX) + reboot allowed kubelet to re-register and pods recovered. After pinning the package in the AMI build and blocking unattended-upgrades, cluster stabilized.

Open follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm AMI bake job includes containerd pin and kernel version check. (assigned to Priya)
- [ ] Add automated smoke test on new nodes that does: kubelet register + run a tiny echo pod + write to PVC. (Diego)
- [ ] Write postmortem (skeleton in confluence link) and update runbook. (Alex)
- [ ] Check other clusters (prod-us, staging) for unattended-upgrades drift. (pagerduty audit)

Notes to self / quick commands to re-run later: (copy/paste friendly)
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector='!node-provision/upgrade-needed'
- ssh ubuntu@$IP sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/containerd.log && scp /tmp/containerd.log me@mybox:/tmp/
- sudo apt-cache policy containerd && dpkg -l | grep containerd
- sudo crictl images --no-trunc
- sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo systemctl start kubelet (careful: disrupts node)
- sudo mount -o remount,rw /var/lib/containerd

Random thought: add a pre-join webhook (lambda) that verifies node kernel & runtime versions against a cluster-approved manifest and rejects join if mismatched. Simpler and safer than forcing package pins post-join.

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating here as we get more logs.
